A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLOAT and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding material can be matched despite renumbering, relocation, and revised presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original HDTF/RAVDESS comparisons, autoencoder experiments including VFHQ, ablations, and a 15-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional pose-editing examples and an analysis of training-data head poses.

M1.justification: v3 adds coefficient-based test-time pose editing while retaining the autoencoder/flow-matching pipeline. Its reported temporal-history procedure uses clean preceding motion latents instead of preceding vector fields, with revised reconstruction targets in Eq. (11). Appendix A.3 also revises the component adversarial loss. These documented procedural changes do not establish that models were retrained.

E1.justification: HDTF, RAVDESS, VFHQ, and the existing painting, Chinese-speech, and singing examples remain. v3 additionally demonstrates editing generated head direction through latent coefficients without external pose-driving signals (Section 5.4, Figure 6), extending the evaluated control task beyond v1's supplied-pose conditioning.

E2.justification: EMO and VASA-1 become qualitative comparators in v3 Figure 12 and Appendix B.2, using their demonstration videos because implementations are unavailable. The quantitative comparator sets, including SadTalker, EDTalk, AniTalker, Hallo, EchoMimic, and the autoencoder comparison with LIA, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a coefficient-intervention test using lambda_15 offsets of ±10 and demonstration-video comparisons with EMO/VASA-1. Existing dataset splits, preprocessing, training budgets, benchmark metrics, and user-study questionnaire remain unchanged. The diffusion baselines' 500 training steps and 50 DDIM sampling steps were already documented in v1.

E4.justification: v3 adds a training-data yaw-distribution analysis supporting the frontal-pose limitation (Figure 15) and a coefficient-editing case study (Figure 6). Existing facial-loss, transformer/diffusion, NFE, guidance, OOD, and failure-case analyses are retained, sometimes relocated or split between figures.

E5.justification: The user study retains the same 15 participants and 95% confidence intervals, and neither version reports additional seed-based uncertainty or significance testing. The new yaw standard deviation describes training-data dispersion rather than uncertainty in model-comparison results.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, ablation, user-study, and FPS values are retained; for example, FLOAT's Table 1 FID remains 21.100/31.681 on HDTF/RAVDESS. New results include pose-editing sequences, demonstration-based EMO/VASA-1 comparisons, and training yaw statistics with mean −0.66° and standard deviation 7.35°.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the conditional Gaussian covariance from t²I to (1−t)²I. v3 adds the assumption that generated latents lie in the learned basis span and derives coefficient recovery by orthogonal projection in Eq. (15). It also revises temporal-history loss equations and changes the component adversarial formula from log Disc(1−D_hat) to −log Disc(D_hat).

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the claimed capabilities to explicit motion editing through the orthogonal latent basis. The first contribution emphasizes reduced sampling steps. The central claims concerning flow-matching generation, temporal consistency, speech-driven emotion, and state-of-the-art performance remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds orthogonality-based reasoning for editing motion coefficients without interfering with other motions. It removes v1's explanations that supplied poses improve distribution matching and that image-derived emotion is less ambiguous. The seven-emotion and frontal-view limitations remain; the yaw histogram supplies new evidence for the existing pose-bias interpretation.

D1.justification: The conditioning diagram changes an audio-processing activation from ReLU to SiLU and the ToScaleShift output from 4h to 6h (v1 Figure 12 versus v3 Figure 18). v3's timing chart explicitly states Hallo's 40 sampling steps. Principal hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and the project URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same 101 works. Research positioning becomes more specific: v3 contrasts its computable orthogonal basis with VASA-1 and connects that structure to editing and flow matching. Section 4.1 also reframes directly employing and scaling LIA as constructing an autoencoder inspired by LIA.

P1.justification: Selected abstract, introduction, and method passages are rewritten, and FMT is generally renamed the frame-wise vector field predictor. Section 5 places applications before ablations, while NFE, guidance, and user-study discussions move into the appendices. Most explanatory prose and the overall section framework remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual organization is substantially reworked. v1 Figure 9 is split into v3 Figures 3 and 10; several tables and qualitative figures move between the main text and appendices. New editing, EMO/VASA-1, and yaw-distribution figures are inserted. The timing chart gains sampling-step and real-time annotations, and the ablation table gains a sampling-step column.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v3 corrects the covariance and component-adversarial-loss formulas, specifies temporal-history targets more clearly, and adds a motion-editing derivation and quantitative support for the pose-bias limitation. These improve technical clarity and evidential support. The gains remain limited: headline results are unchanged, added baseline comparisons use demonstrations, and Appendix A.1 introduces an identity/motion-latent notation inconsistency.
